protocol.description: Effects flame draws for a surface, the way it draws its own: glass behind a surface's translucent content. An app only describes them, flame draws them, with whatever is behind the surface right then.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects made from it stay as they are.

entry.name: glass_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a glass object

request.name: get_glass
request.description: A glass object for the surface, one per surface. A second one is the glass_exists error.

interface.name: flame_glass_v1

description.summary: panes of glass behind a surface

interface.description:
Rounded panes of glass behind the surface's content: what's behind the surface is blurred, its colors pushed, tinted, bent at the pane's edge and lit along its rim, then the surface's own pixels go over it. A pane shows through wherever the surface's content is translucent.
The panes are double buffered state: clear and add_pane change the pending set, wl_surface.commit makes it current. Coordinates are surface local, lengths in surface local units. Panes are clipped to the surface.
If the surface is destroyed the object goes inert.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Its panes go with the surface's next commit.

request.name: set_shape

description.summary: the window is a rounded shape of its own

request.description:
The surface is a whole window that draws its own rounded edge: its corners rounded by radius, outside them nothing. flame draws no border around it then. 0 (the start) for a plain window, flame's border around it.
Double buffered like the panes, made current by wl_surface.commit. Only a window's main surface means anything by it.

request.name: add_pane
request.description:
A pane added to the pending set, drawn after the ones before it.
tint is straight (not premultiplied) 0xRRGGBBAA, laid over the blur. saturation 1 keeps the colors behind it, more makes them vivid. edge is how much light its rim catches, 0 for none. refraction is how far its rim bends what's behind it, 0 for none.

request.name: set_opacity

description.summary: how much of the glass shows

request.description:
All of the surface's panes faded together, blur, tint and rim alike: 1 (the start) for all of them, 0 for none. For glass that comes and goes with what's drawn over it.
Double buffered like the panes, made current by wl_surface.commit.
